subject: Clarify SOC 2 / CAIQ overlap for EMEA VPC carve-in and subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: security@nimbus-sys.com (Nimbus Systems)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orion-fin.com, security-team@greenleafinsurance.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II + CAIQ: EMEA VPC coverage and subprocessor attestations

Hi Kimberly,

GreenLeaf’s security team asked us to validate a few things ahead of the production integration. Quick ask: can Redwood provide your most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a completed CAIQ/SIG summary for the EMEA VPC deployment? Specifically we need confirmation on: 

- Whether Redwood considers the EMEA VPC a "carve-in" to the hosted environment (i.e., within the scope of Redwood's SOC 2) or if customers should expect a carve-out scenario that requires additional bridge letters.
- If Redwood’s SOC 2 covers the cloud provider responsibilities relevant to key controls (KMS key management, snapshot backups, snapshot encryption, and network segmentation) for the EMEA region, or whether we should expect separate cloud provider reports (e.g., AWS/Azure SOC) to be provided by Redwood.
- A subprocessor inventory and the latest attestations for subprocessors with access to customer data in the EMEA region (including whether any subprocessors hold custodial KMS keys).
- Any current or planned bridge letters for the 2026 audit period that would explicitly mention regional carve-in semantics.

We’d prefer PDFs we can attach to our internal evidence tracker and a short SSP excerpt describing how Redwood maps shared responsibility for EMEA VPCs. Can you also confirm a point of contact for a 30-minute technical walkthrough?

Attachments we’d like: SOC 2 Type II report (2026), CAIQ/Alt SIG spreadsheet, subprocessor CSV, and any bridge letter drafts. Thanks — tight timeline, so a response by EOD Friday (6/4) would be ideal.

Best,
Ari Patel
Security Analyst, Nimbus Systems
security@nimbus-sys.com

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II + CAIQ: EMEA VPC coverage and subprocessor attestations

Thanks Ari — appreciate the clear checklist. Marina tagging Marissa (Privacy & Compliance) and Karthik (Infra) to help. High-level answers up front: 

- Redwood treats customer VPCs in our managed EMEA offering as within Redwood’s control plane scope for the purposes of our SOC 2 (i.e., we provide a carve-in path) when customers opt into our managed VPC offering and agree to the data residency addendum. That was reflected in the 2026 Type II scope for EMEA customers who purchased managed VPC.
- The SOC 2 covers Redwood-managed controls; cloud provider controls remain dependent on the cloud provider's SOC/assurance reports. We will provide a mapping that shows which SOC 2 controls rely on the cloud provider’s attestations and where Redwood adds compensating controls (e.g., KMS usage policies, snapshot lifecycle policies).
- I'll attach the SOC 2 PDF, the subprocessor inventory (CSV), and a short SSP summary for the EMEA VPC carve-in. For CAIQ/SIG we have a completed baseline CAIQ export; Marissa will add a quick matrix highlighting the CAIQ answers relevant to EMEA data residency and key management.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll circulate the requested PDFs and CSV now (attached).
2) Karthik and I can run a 30-minute SSP walkthrough tomorrow (6/4) at 10:00 AM BST / 02:00 AM PDT — propose 30 minutes; we can shift if that time doesn't work.
3) If GreenLeaf needs an explicit bridge letter calling out the carve-in language for audit continuity, we can prepare a draft for legal review and share a target timeline.

I’m attaching the reports now. If you need the raw cloud provider SOCs, we can either link them or include the relevant excerpts — let us know preference.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance (Redwood Inference)
kimberly_park@redwood.com

On Thu, Jun 3, 2027 at 11:04 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kimberly: attaching SOC and SSP excerpts.

Quick technical notes to clarify the mapping: 

- KMS: Redwood-managed KMS instances in the EMEA region are customer-dedicated keys (we use customer key material via our KMS integration where customers opt-in). Subprocessors do NOT hold custodial keys unless explicitly contracted and documented in the subprocessor CSV. The CSV includes a column "kms_custody" with yes/no flags.
- Snapshots: All managed snapshot lifecycle operations enforce encryption-at-rest using provider-managed encryption keys by default; when customers enable bring-your-own-key (BYOK), snapshots are tied to the customer KMS. We log snapshot exports and produce audit events to the Redwood audit log (retention per the EMEA policy in SSP).
- Network segmentation: For managed VPCs, ingress/egress is controlled by our managed gateway and customer-configured security groups. The SSP excerpt includes the network diagram and control IDs that map to SOC control narratives.
- Cloud provider SOCs: We reference provider SOCs (AWS EU reports) for low-level infra controls; we will include links to the relevant provider reports in the Drive folder. We do not re-issue provider SOCs; we provide mapping and excerpts that indicate which controls we rely on.

Drive folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cEXAMPLE-ssp-eu
HubSpot record for GreenLeaf: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890

I’m available for the walkthrough tomorrow; suggest 10:00 AM BST is fine.
